acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p jmap-mail-server --features sieve passes; all 17 integration tests pass; test oracles are spec examples not code output
description:
Write integration tests in tests/sieve_integration.rs. Test oracles are spec JSON examples from draft-ietf-jmap-sieve-22 §2.3–§2.6 — NOT the code under test.

WHAT: Full integration test coverage for all four SieveScript methods.

ALGORITHM:
1. Create tests/sieve_integration.rs with:
   #![cfg(feature = "sieve")]
   mod common;
   use common::MemoryBackend;
   use jmap_mail_server::{handle_sieve_get, handle_sieve_set, handle_sieve_query, handle_sieve_validate};
   use jmap_types::Id;

2. Test helper: async fn setup_sieve_account(backend: &MemoryBackend) -> Id
   - Creates account "sieve-account-1"
   - Uploads a valid script blob (e.g., b"keep;" — minimally valid Sieve per RFC 5228 §8)
   - Returns (account_id, blob_id)

3. Individual test functions (all #[tokio::test] async):

   sieve_get_no_scripts: fresh account, SieveScript/get returns empty list
   Oracle: { "list": [], "notFound": [], "state": "0" }

   sieve_set_create_basic: upload blob, create script with name "my-filter"
   Oracle: created["A"] has id, name=="my-filter", isActive==false (spec §2.4.1 example 6 shape)

   sieve_set_create_name_null: create with name=null, server assigns a name
   Oracle: created["A"].name is Some non-empty string (spec §2.4.1 example 6)

   sieve_set_create_and_activate: create + onSuccessActivateScript="#A"
   Oracle: created["A"].isActive==true (spec §2.4.1 example 6 explicitly shows this)

   sieve_set_at_most_one_active: create two scripts S1 and S2, activate S2
   Oracle: S1 appears in updated with isActive:false; S2 in created/updated with isActive:true

   sieve_set_deactivate_only: on_success_deactivate_script=true, one active script
   Oracle: updated[S1.id] = {"isActive": false} (spec §2.4.1 example 8)

   sieve_set_reactivate: on_success_activate_script=S1.id on inactive script
   Oracle: updated[S1.id] = {"isActive": true} (spec §2.4.1 example 9)

   sieve_set_destroy_active_rejected: sieveIsActive error
   Oracle: notDestroyed[S1.id]["type"] == "sieveIsActive"

   sieve_set_duplicate_name: two creates with same name in same request OR create that conflicts with existing
   Oracle: notCreated["B"]["type"] == "alreadyExists"; notCreated["B"]["existingId"] == S1.id

   sieve_get_by_id: SieveScript/get with ids=[S1.id], returns list with one entry, notFound empty
   Oracle: list[0] fields match stored script

   sieve_get_not_found: SieveScript/get with ids=[nonexistent-id], list empty, notFound has the id
   Oracle: notFound == ["nonexistent-id"]

   sieve_query_all: SieveScript/query with no filter, all scripts in ids
   Oracle: all inserted script ids appear in result

   sieve_query_filter_active: filter {"isActive": true}, only active script in ids

   sieve_validate_valid: blob = b"keep;", error==null
   Oracle: spec §2.6 response shape { accountId, error: null }

   sieve_validate_invalid: blob = b"this is not sieve", error.type=="invalidSieve"
   Oracle: spec §2.6 response shape { accountId, error: {type: "invalidSieve", description: "..."}  }
   Note: MemoryBackend validates as valid for non-empty UTF-8, so inject an empty blob to trigger the error path

   sieve_get_unknown_account: accountNotFound
   sieve_set_unknown_account: accountNotFound
   sieve_validate_unknown_account: accountNotFound

DEFENSIVE RULES (test code):
- Test oracles come from spec examples, NOT from running the implementation and capturing output
- .expect() is acceptable in test setup helpers (failure = bug in test environment)
- Never modify tests to make them pass — fix the implementation instead
- Valid Sieve script for tests: b"keep;" (RFC 5228 §8 example, independent oracle)

AGENT TEAM: Implementer (who writes tests) + Validator (who runs them and reports failures)

TESTS: cargo test -p jmap-mail-server --features sieve -- --test sieve_integration passes; all 17 named tests pass
design:
Test file: tests/sieve_integration.rs (compiled only with cfg(feature=sieve)).

Tests to write:

get_all_scripts: exercise draft §2.3.1 example 1 — insert known script into MemorySieveBackend, call SieveScript/get with no ids, verify list and state fields match expected.

get_by_id: fetch one script by id, verify all fields including blobId and isActive.

get_not_found: fetch nonexistent id, appears in notFound not list.

set_create_and_activate: create a script, set on_success_activate_script to its creation ref (#0), verify response has isActive: true in created entry (draft §2.4.1).

set_swap_active: with two scripts where A is active, set request creates/updates nothing but sets on_success_activate_script to B's id; verify A.isActive becomes false, B.isActive becomes true in updated map.

set_deactivate: on_success_deactivate_script: true with no other mutations; verify active script is in updated with isActive: false.

set_destroy_active_rejected: attempt to destroy the active script directly (without deactivating first); verify sieveIsActive SetError.

set_name_collision: create two scripts with same name; verify alreadyExists SetError with existingId field.

query_all: query with no filter, verify all ids returned.

query_active_only: filter isActive: true, verify only active script id returned.

query_sort_by_name: multiple scripts, sort ascending by name, verify order.

validate_valid: upload a minimal valid script blob (require []; keep;), call SieveScript/validate, verify error: null.

validate_invalid: upload a blob with invalid Sieve content (e.g. garbled bytes), verify error.type == invalidSieve.

vacationresponse_protected: mark a script as the VR-backed script, attempt destroy and content update, verify forbidden SetError both times.
